author: TOM HALEY Staff Writer
title: Castleton drops both ends of LEC opener | Local | rutlandherald.com
text:
CASTLETON — The Vermont State University basketball teams lost both games in Wednesday night's Little East Conference opening doubleheader but the Spartan women were locked in a tie with Keene State at halftime.
The Spartans led the Owls 18-15 after the first quarter and were deadlocked 33-33 at the half, but Keene State asserted itself in the second 20 minutes to leave Glenbrook Gym with a 76-65 victory.
Keene State senior forward Avery Stewart said the Owls didn't change much at halftime, just turned up the intensity.
"Our identity is effort and energy," Stewart said.
Balanced scoring carried the Owls. Brynn Rautiola led four Owls in double figures with 19 points, Ruby Dasaro, a Vermonter from Fairfield, followed with 17 points, Stewart tossed in 15 and Sydney Cassidy 13.
Proctor's Maggie McKearin led the Spartans with 16 points and again displayed accuracy from 3-point land where she made three of her five of her long range shots. Stasia Epler and Kyrielle Deuso followed her with 15 and 13 points, respectively.
The Spartans were still very much in the game midway through the fourth quarter. When Epler scored inside and Deuso drove hard to the hoop for another bucket, the four straight points pared the Owls' lead to three, 59-56.
That is why the next hoop by Rautiola was so big, giving the Owls some breathing room. They pulled away to the double-digit victory from there.
"It is all about getting in people's faces for us," Keene State coach Keith Boucher said.
"I thought Castleton played hard, but we made some big shots."
The Spartans' record dropped to 3-3 as they got off to an 0-1 start in the LEC. The Owls go to 6-2 and 1-0.
"There are no easy games in this conference and we all know each other. Any win on the road in this conference is a good win," Boucher said.
McKearin had a strong game with five rebounds and three assists to go with her 16 points.
Emily Adams grabbed a game-high 11 rebounds to lead VTSU Castleton's rebounding advantage, 37-28.
Nevaeh Camp, by way of Burr and Burton Academy, also had a productive game with nine points and seven rebounds.
The Spartans will play their second LEC game on Saturday at UMass Dartmouth. Their next home contest comes on Dec. 10 when SUNY Cobleskill, with first-year player Kate Hadwen from Fair Haven, comes to town.
There was a familiar face in the stands. Meghan O'Sullivan scored 1,147 points for the Castleton women's basketball team from 2011 through 2015.
She is now on the coaching staff at Mount Mansfield Union High School and the Cougars came to Glenbrook to watch because VTSU Castleton and Keene State each had a Mount Mansfield graduate on the team. Representing the Cougars for Castleton was Brianna Brownell and MMU graduate Bella Schultz-Mitchell was wearing the Keene State red.
The MMU team held a practice before the game in the SHAPE Gym adjacent to Glenbrook.
Keene State breezed in the men's game. The Owls won 87-65 but had the game pretty much salted away by halftime with a 53-28 advantage.
Will Radcliff led the Spartans with 26 points and Ben Seiler added 10..
The Spartans hit the road on Saturday and will hope to improve their Little East stock against UMass Dartmouth. The men's next home game comes on Dec. 9 against SUNY Cobleskill.
